{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the framing of the dictator game (giving vs. taking) would have asymmetric effects on the allocation behavior of male and female dictators, despite no overall difference in aggregate allocations.",
  "design": "between",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Dictator game frame: 'Giving' (dictator decides how much of £10 to give to recipient) vs. 'Taking' (recipient has £10, dictator decides how much to take for themselves).",
  "outcome_measure": "Amount allocated to the recipient (in the giving frame, the amount given; in the taking frame, £10 minus the amount taken).",
  "population_and_setting": "University students at the University of East Anglia, participating in a computerized laboratory experiment.",
  "sample_size_total": 280,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via ORSEE; participants received a £3 show-up fee plus earnings from the game.",
  "analysis_plan": "Mann-Whitney tests and OLS regressions comparing allocations between frames, including interaction terms for gender and treatment, and Probit models to analyze the distribution of 'selfish' (allocating 0) and 'egalitarian' (allocating half) types.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used a balanced pool of 35 male and 35 female dictators per treatment (140 total dictators). Recipients were passive. A secondary task involving guessing the dictator's decision was included for recipients but is not the focus of the focal effect."
}
